abstract: In the context of the rapid development of digital technology, the construction industry has also ushered in unprecedented changes. The wide application of AI and digital technology has significantly improved the production efficiency of the construction industry, but also put forward new requirements for the skill level of workers in the construction industry. However, as an important force in rural construction, workers in the rural construction industry are often relatively inadequate in skill level and knowledge reserve, which is difficult to adapt to the development needs of digital construction. [l]This leads to the rural construction industry in a disadvantageous position in the competition, hindering the prosperity and development of rural economy. In order to improve the practical ability of rural construction industry workers, many regions have begun to explore the construction of AI digital sharing training bases. Through the introduction of advanced digital equipment and technology, these training bases provide practical platforms for rural construction industry workers, so that they can personally experience the construction and management process of digital buildings. Through practice, they can master advanced construction skills and improve their competitiveness, so as to better adapt to the development needs of digital architecture. The purpose of this study is to deeply explore the promotion effect of the construction of AI digital sharing training base on the practice path of rural construction industry workers. Through field investigation and case analysis, this study will reveal the positive role of the training base in improving the practical ability of rural construction industry workers, promoting rural economic development, and promoting the digital development of rural construction industry. At the same time, this study will also provide reference for the practice and research in related fields, and contribute to the sustainable development of rural construction industry.

articleTitle: Optimization Design and Performance Research of 5G P-IOT Passive Tags Based on LPWAN and Transformer in Long Range Coverage Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science, Electronic Information Engineering and Intelligent Control Technology (CEI)
abstract: With the expansion of the Internet of Things (Io'T), current passive IoT (P-IoT) systems supporting 5G are facing challenges such as limited communication range, high interference, and low data throughput in complex environments. This paper introduces E-TransLPWAN (LPWAN optimization framework based on enhanced transformers), a novel solution for monitoring ultra-high voltage (UHV) power grids. This framework solves the above problems by optimizing spectrum utilization and power control, while effectively processing large-scale time series data using Transformer's self-attention mechanism. The experimental results show that E-TransLPWAN can significantly improve the performance of existing models, including a 50% reduction in latency, a 6% increase in anomaly detection accuracy (reaching 97%), and a 30% reduction in energy consumption. These improvements have enhanced the reliability and cost-effectiveness of UHV monitoring and ensuring the stability of the power grid.

articleTitle: Visual SLAM with 3D Gaussian Primitives and Depth Priors Enabling Novel View Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science, Electronic Information Engineering and Intelligent Control Technology (CEI)
abstract: Conventional geometry-based SLAM systems lack dense 3D reconstruction capabilities since their data association usually relies on feature correspondences. Additionally, learning-based SLAM systems often fall short in terms of real-time performance and accuracy. Balancing real-time performance with dense 3D reconstruction capabilities is a challenging problem. In this paper, we present a real-time RGB-D SLAM system that uses 3D Gaussian Splatting for both 3D scene representation and pose estimation. This method enables efficient real-time rendering and differentiable optimization through CUDA, offering an edge over NeRF. We also enable mesh reconstruction from 3D Gaussians for explicit dense 3D reconstruction. To estimate accurate camera poses, we utilize a rotation-translation decoupled strategy with inverse optimization. This involves iteratively updating both in several iterations through gradient-based optimization. This process includes differentiably rendering RGB, depth, and silhouette maps and updating the camera parameters to minimize a combined loss of photometric loss, depth geometry loss, and visibility loss, given the existing 3D Gaussian map. However, 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) struggles to accurately represent surfaces due to the multi-view inconsistency of 3D Gaussians, which can lead to reduced accuracy in both camera pose estimation and scene reconstruction. To address this, we utilize depth priors as additional regularization to enforce geometric constraints, thereby improving the accuracy of both pose estimation and 3D reconstruction. We also provide extensive experimental results on public benchmark datasets to demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods in terms of pose accuracy, geometric accuracy, and rendering performance.

articleTitle: The Iterative Query Knowledge Graph Completion Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science, Electronic Information Engineering and Intelligent Control Technology (CEI)
abstract: Film knowledge graphs have been an essential information resource in the film industry. However, due to the rapid update and complexity of film information, completing these graphs has remained a challenge. Particularly in an open-world context, the completion of film knowledge graphs must account for various unknown factors and uncertainties. This paper provides a comprehensive summary of the constraints and logical rules in the film domain and organizes a basic information database related to personnel in the film industry for the first time. A novel strategy for completing film knowledge graphs was proposed to address gaps and enhance their quality and usability. The approach integrated the deep understanding of large language models with domain-specific expertise in the film industry, achieving an efficient and accurate completion process through pre-screening, individual prediction, and the integration of external databases. Experiments were conducted on the established film knowledge graph MetaQA, and a new dataset, MetaQA-Latest Additions, was created to test the method's performance with new film information. Baseline comparisons and rigorous data analysis validated the effectiveness of the proposed method, yielding competitive results. This work provides a robust tool for constructing and updating film knowledge graphs, potentially offering better support for applications such as film recommendation, content analysis, and industry research.

articleTitle: Improved Sine-cosine Algorithm for Achievable Rate Maximization in IRS Assisted Indoor VLC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science, Electronic Information Engineering and Intelligent Control Technology (CEI)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) based on the mirror array is regarded as an effective way to increase the stability of indoor visible light communication (VLC) links, which can combat the blocking problem of line of sight (LoS) link and improve the systems achievable communication rate. The achievable rate maximization problem that mirror array based IRS assisted indoor VLC systems is a highly non-convex optimization problem. We propose an improved Sine cosine Algorithm (SCA) to solve the achievable rate maximization problem in which the practical random position state information of the users and the access point (AP) is considered. We propose a two-step iterative strategy for the improved SCA. In the first stage of iteration, the control mechanism of random parameters is improved to adjust the algorithm ability in the search. In the second stage of iteration, a fast search and comparison mechanism is introduced, which can avoid the improved SCA to get a local optimal solution. The simulation shows that the improved SCA is superior to the traditional SCA in convergence and efficiency.

articleTitle: Differentially Private Geographic and Energy-Aware Routing Protocol
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Computer Science, Electronic Information Engineering and Intelligent Control Technology (CEI)
abstract: With the development and application of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), privacy protection issues are becoming increasingly prominent but are not well studied. In this paper, we introduce differential privacy to the routing of the WSN, study the location-based routing protocol: Geographic and Energy-Aware Routing (GEAR), and propose an improved Differentially Private GEAR (DP-GEAR) protocol via the exponential mechanism to protect the geographic routing privacy of WSN. Theoretical results show that our proposed DP-GEAR protocol guarantees ε-Differential Privacy (ε-DP) and experimental results show that the routing performance of DP-GEAR is similar to the traditional GEAR protocol, with more balanced energy consumption, which means that the privacy enhancement does not come at the expense of the routing performance.
